summary.sentence: Fixes upstream issue `MessagePack-CSharp#2283`: the source generator and the analyzer no longer crash when one of your types has a member whose type is a generic struct from a referenced assembly.
The crash fix works: the issue's repro now gets a generated resolver and formatters, and its bytes on the wire are unchanged.

The PR also does a second thing the issue did not ask for: it stops reporting problems found in referenced types, which turns an existing build error into silence and lets a formatter that drops a value ship.

cases.title: Case 1 · Referenced generic class with an unkeyed member (the warning above)
cases.story: **Cause and effect:** the model, the generated files and the run-time behaviour are identical on both sides. The only hand-off that differs is ②: the filter removes the error. So the same formatter that loses `Unkeyed` used to be blocked by a failing build and now ships.

cases.title: Case 2 · The issue's repro

cases.title: Case 3 · Referenced generic struct with an unkeyed member
cases.story: **Cause and effect:** two causes act here. The crash fix at ① makes the generator produce files. The filter at ② removes the `MsgPack004` error that was reported just before the crash. Together they turn a failing build into a passing one that drops `Unkeyed`.

requirements.statement: The source generator no longer crashes with IndexOutOfRangeException when a member's type is a closed generic struct from a referenced assembly.
The analyzer no longer crashes (AD0001) on the same input.
A generated resolver and formatters are produced for such types.
Diagnostics for types declared in the project itself are unchanged.

symptom.why: The issue reports the generator and analyzer throwing IndexOutOfRangeException while collecting the type.

found.statement: For a referenced generic type with an unkeyed member, the `MsgPack004` build error is gone, and the formatter that now ships loses that member's value.
The crash fix does not need the new filter: the PR built without the filter line still generates code for the issue's repro and still reports `MsgPack004` for the referenced class.
The crash is fixed: the issue's repro used to throw in the type collector and now gets a model and generated code.

Only one of the two null-safe lookups is the crash fix: without line 1077 the issue's repro throws again, while without line 985 every input gives the same result, so no input here shows what the second lookup changes.
You can stop worrying about the wire format of the issue's repro and about diagnostics for your own types: both are identical before and after.

decisions.question: Should problems found inside referenced types stop being reported?
decisions.detail: The issue asks only for no crash and a generated resolver. The PR also drops every diagnostic located outside the project being compiled, which silences `MsgPack004` for referenced generic types; the author's third test asserts that silence as expected.
decisions.wouldSettleIt: A maintainer's statement of the reporting policy for types from packages the user does not build.
options: Keep the silence: the assembly that defines the type reports it, if it is built with the analyzer
Keep only the crash fix and drop the filter
Report such problems as a warning on the member that uses the type

decisions.question: Does the generated formatter work in a trimmed or NativeAOT app, where the issue's harm actually occurs?
decisions.detail: The probe runs the generated code on .NET 8 with the JIT. A trimmed or NativeAOT publish was not built.
decisions.wouldSettleIt: A NativeAOT publish of the issue's repro that round-trips an object through the generated resolver.
options: Run that publish in CI before merging

decisions.question: In an IDE with project references, are diagnostics for a referenced project's types now dropped too?
decisions.detail: The filter forwards a diagnostic only if its location is in a syntax tree of the compilation being analyzed, so a type from another project in the same solution is filtered as well. Nothing here runs a multi-project workspace.
decisions.wouldSettleIt: A two-project Roslyn workspace test, or a check in Visual Studio with a project reference.
options: Accept it as part of the policy decision above
